item.content: {"url": "https://api.openalex.org/works?search=role+of+episodic+memory+in+long-term+preference+formation+and+reinforcement+learning&per-page=4&select=id%2Cdoi%2Ctitle%2Cpublication_year%2Ctype%2Ccited_by_count%2Copen_access%2Cprimary_location%2Cabstract_inverted_index", "scope": "OpenAlex scholarly metadata and reconstructed abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/W2970567787\", \"doi\": \"https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.1910.13406\", \"title\": \"Generalization of Reinforcement Learners with Working and Episodic Memory\", \"publication_year\": 2019, \"type\": \"preprint\", \"cited_by_count\": 35, \"open_access\": {\"is_oa\": true, \"oa_status\": \"green\", \"oa_url\": \"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.13406\", \"any_repository_has_fulltext\": true}, \"primary_location\": {\"id\": \"pmh:oai:arXiv.org:1910.13406\", \"doi\": null, \"is_oa\": true, \"landing_page_url\": \"http://arxiv.org/abs/1910.13406\", \"pdf_url\": \"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.13406\", \"source\": {\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/S4306400194\", \"display_name\": \"arXiv (Cornell University)\", \"issn_l\": \"2331-8422\", \"issn\": [\"2331-8422\"], \"is_oa\": true, \"is_in_doaj\": false, \"is_core\": false, \"listed_in\": [], \"host_organization\": \"https://openalex.org/I205783295\", \"host_organization_name\": \"Cornell University\", \"host_organization_lineage\": [\"https://openalex.org/I205783295\"], \"host_organization_lineage_names\": [], \"type\": \"repository\"}, \"license\": null, \"license_id\": null, \"version\": \"submittedVersion\", \"is_accepted\": false, \"is_published\": false, \"raw_source_name\": null, \"raw_type\": \"text\"}, \"abstract\": \"Memory is an important aspect of intelligence and plays a role in many deep reinforcement learning models. However, little progress has been made in understanding when specific memory systems help more than others and how well they generalize. The field also has yet to see a prevalent consistent and rigorous approach for evaluating agent performance on holdout data. In this paper, we aim to develop a comprehensive methodology to test different kinds of memory in an agent and assess how well the agent can apply what it learns in training to a holdout set that differs from the training set along dimensions that we suggest are relevant for evaluating memory-specific generalization.
